office.name: The Overcoat Edit
office.description: Tonal winter warmth — refined and ready for the LIRR
office.stylist_note: Knot the scarf in a relaxed Paris knot — cross and tuck one end underneath. Let the turtleneck peek just above the coat collar. Keep the topcoat buttoned all the way up except the last button. The entire look should read as one clean silhouette.

office.name: The Dark Navy Stack
office.description: Navy overcoat and black turtleneck — a winter uniform with quiet authority
office.stylist_note: The all-dark palette needs clean lines — no bunching at the waist. Tuck the turtleneck into the trousers. Keep the overcoat fully buttoned on the commute. Black belt, black shoes: commit to the monochrome. The navy coat over black is intentional contrast, not a mistake.

office.name: The Earth Tone Winter
office.description: Warm brown topcoat over oatmeal — every layer earthy and considered
office.stylist_note: Brown topcoat over an oatmeal turtleneck is a rarely-seen move that pays off big. Keep the trousers in the tan-camel family to stay in the palette. Tan suede loafers finish it. This works because every element is one color story.

office.name: The Grey Column
office.description: Tonal grey from coat to shoe — the easiest hard look to pull off
office.stylist_note: Grey topcoat over light grey merino only works when the tones are sufficiently different — mid-grey coat, light grey sweater, charcoal trouser. The gradient matters. Black chelsea boots anchor the whole thing. Don't add color: the restraint is the point.

office.name: The Cable Knit Office
office.description: Cream cable knit under a structured wool coat — texture with authority
office.stylist_note: The cable knit turtleneck is a statement — wear it with a clean, structure topcoat so it reads deliberate. Full tuck into slim navy trousers. Cognac Oxford shoes ground the cream-on-navy. This is a rare look that signals confidence and individuality.

weekend.name: The Deep Freeze
weekend.description: Rugged warmth with considered texture for a cold Port Saturday
weekend.stylist_note: The sherpa jacket is the statement here — let it be. Keep everything underneath simple and dark. Tuck the henley into the jeans for a hint of intention even in casual mode. Lace the duck boots loosely.

weekend.name: The Waxed Wool Combo
weekend.description: Waxed canvas over a heavy crewneck — the weekend uniform for serious cold
weekend.stylist_note: The chunky oatmeal crewneck under a waxed jacket is a texture collision that works because the silhouettes are different — boxy canvas over a fitted knit. Dark jeans, white sneakers. The sneakers keep it from reading too rugged.

weekend.name: The Shearling Saturday
weekend.description: Shearling collar jacket over a heavyweight henley — warmth that looks intentional
weekend.stylist_note: The shearling jacket is the whole look — build everything else around it simply. Dark jeans, simple tan work boots. Don't compete with the jacket texture: henley stays plain and untucked. Lace the boots loosely for a relaxed silhouette.

weekend.name: The Navy Wool Dad
weekend.description: Navy wool overshirt over a cream henley — smart without trying
weekend.stylist_note: The navy wool overshirt wears like a shirt jacket — leave it unbuttoned over the cream henley so the contrast shows. Roll the jeans once. Cream sneakers echo the henley and keep the bottom half clean. This reads effortlessly composed.

weekend.name: The Field Jacket Freeze
weekend.description: Military field jacket layered over a chunky turtleneck — utility with intention
weekend.stylist_note: Field jacket over a turtleneck is a classic cold-weather pairing. Leave the jacket open so the turtleneck shows fully. Dark jeans, brown boots. The olive-oatmeal-indigo palette is understated and deliberate. Roll the jeans once.

office.name: The Warm Monday
office.description: Intentional layering for a considered office entry
office.stylist_note: Pop the collar of the OCBD above the quarter-zip — just the collar tips visible above the ribbing. Tuck both layers into the trousers for a clean silhouette. Roll the trouser cuffs one clean fold. The chore jacket wears open at the office, closed on the commute.

office.name: East Coast Prep
office.description: The timeless preppy formula — elevated for fintech
office.stylist_note: Layer the forest green crewneck over the oxford with the collar and 3–4 inches of cuffs showing. Tuck both layers. Leave the topcoat slightly open and let it drape naturally. Carry it over your arm on the train for commuter-cool credibility.

office.name: The Navy Chore Office
office.description: Navy chore jacket over a white mock-neck — modern workwear with restraint
office.stylist_note: The navy chore jacket over a white mock-neck turtleneck is clean and architectural. Keep the jacket buttoned at the office. Slate blue trousers maintain the cool palette. Dark brown derbies ground it without going formal.

office.name: The Merino Stack
office.description: Dark merino crewneck under a topcoat — maximum warmth, zero fuss
office.stylist_note: Dark navy merino crewneck under a camel topcoat is a classic pairing. Keep the merino fully tucked. The camel and navy combination works because they're in opposite corners of the color wheel. Cognac boots tie the warm tones together.

office.name: The Burgundy Layer
office.description: Burgundy merino v-neck and olive field jacket — unexpected and considered
office.stylist_note: Burgundy and olive is a rich, unexpected combination that reads intellectual rather than preppy. Layer the v-neck over the OCBD with collar fully visible. Field jacket open at the office. Charcoal trousers keep the color story grounded.

weekend.name: The Saturday Routine
weekend.description: Waxed canvas and denim — weekend-ready without overthinking it
weekend.stylist_note: The waxed jacket should look lived-in — that's the point. Untucked henley, loose but intentional. Roll the jeans twice for a clean break above the ankle. White sneakers keep the whole look from reading too rugged.

weekend.name: The Weekend Knit
weekend.description: The shawl cardigan as outerwear — old-school prep done right
weekend.stylist_note: Keep the cardigan open with the Breton tee showing fully. Don't button it — that's the move. The Breton tee stripe adds visual interest without trying. Roll the chino cuffs once. Suede loafers are the understated finisher.

weekend.name: The Field Jacket Dad
weekend.description: Olive field jacket over a navy henley — utility cool for a cold Saturday
weekend.stylist_note: Field jacket open, henley showing underneath. Roll the jeans once at the ankle. Tan boots ground the olive-navy palette with warmth. This outfit takes five seconds to think about and looks like you thought about it for hours.

weekend.name: The Chore Casual
weekend.description: Navy chore jacket and white crew tee — workwear made weekend
weekend.stylist_note: Navy chore jacket over a white tee is the most versatile weekend layer you own. Leave it unbuttoned, tee untucked. Dark jeans, clean white sneakers. The structure of the chore jacket keeps it from reading sloppy — even fully casual.

weekend.name: The Tobacco Overshirt
weekend.description: Tobacco knit overshirt over a cream tee — rich color, effortless structure
weekend.stylist_note: Wear the tobacco overshirt unbuttoned as a relaxed layer over a plain cream tee. Dark jeans and cognac boots keep the warm color story consistent. Roll the jeans once. The tobacco-cream-cognac trio is understated but unmistakably intentional.

office.name: The Considered Entry
office.description: Knit polo under a chore jacket — effortless and intentional
office.stylist_note: Leave the chore jacket open — let the knit polo's texture do the work. Tuck the polo into the trousers for a clean waist. No belt. The tobacco brown-on-tobacco-brown tonal pairing is deliberate and strong. Black Chelsea boots ground the earth tones perfectly.

office.name: Sweater Vest Season
office.description: The vest that reads boardroom without trying too hard
office.stylist_note: Wear the OCBD with only the top button open under the vest. Tuck the shirt crisply — this one demands a full tuck. Roll the cuffs of the OCBD once, so they show just below the vest. The slate blue/white/stone palette is classic and refreshingly clean.

office.name: The Unstructured Layer
office.description: Olive blouson over a white OCBD — casual structure for a mild office day
office.stylist_note: The olive blouson jacket reads relaxed but purposeful. Leave it unzipped. OCBD tucked into the navy trousers, one button open at collar. Cognac leather loafers add warmth to the olive-white-navy palette. An effortless cool-weather look for fintech.

office.name: The Earth Tone Office
office.description: Tan chore jacket over an army green knit polo — tonal and quietly sharp
office.stylist_note: Tan and army green is a rich earth-tone pairing that reads intentional in a fintech office. Chore jacket open, polo tucked. Stone trousers keep the warm palette going without becoming muddy. Brown suede loafers close the look.

office.name: The Navy Workwear Office
office.description: Navy chore jacket over a grey mock-neck — clean, modern, no fuss
office.stylist_note: Navy chore jacket over a light grey mock-neck is architectural and clean. Keep the jacket buttoned. Dark navy trousers maintain the cool palette. Cognac boots are the one warm note that stops it reading cold. This is the anti-blazer office look.

weekend.name: The Overshirt Layer
weekend.description: Textured knit overshirt over a clean tee — controlled casual
weekend.stylist_note: Wear the overshirt unbuttoned as a layer — it reads like a shirt jacket without the formality. Dark jeans keep the bottom half grounded. Chelsea boots elevate the denim just enough. This is the off-duty exec look.

weekend.name: The Chore Dad
weekend.description: Tan chore jacket, navy henley, dark jeans — the dad uniform done right
weekend.stylist_note: Tan chore jacket open over a navy henley: the jacket's warm tone lifts the dark palette. Untucked henley. Roll the jeans once. White sneakers keep it fresh. This is the outfit that makes other dads at the park ask where you shop.

weekend.name: The Trucker Weekend
weekend.description: Olive denim trucker jacket and dark jeans — casual American done sharp
weekend.stylist_note: Olive trucker jacket over a plain cream OCBD — leave the jacket open, shirt un-tucked. Dark jeans rolled once. Tan work boots keep the palette warm. This is the perfectly curated 'I just threw this on' look.

weekend.name: The Navy Sweat Layer
weekend.description: Navy crewneck sweatshirt under a tobacco overshirt — the relaxed-smart paradox
weekend.stylist_note: Tobacco overshirt unbuttoned over a heavy navy crewneck sweatshirt. No logos on the sweatshirt — this only works with a clean piece. Dark jeans, white leather sneakers. Roll the jeans once. The contrast of warm tobacco against cool navy is what makes this look work.

weekend.name: The Harrington
weekend.description: Retro-prep cool — a Harrington jacket earned its place here
weekend.stylist_note: Zip the Harrington to about mid-chest and let the white tee show at the neckline. Roll the chinos once — one clean fold. White leather sneakers make the whole thing read young and put-together simultaneously. This outfit works everywhere from brunch to the hardware store.

office.name: The Spring Office
office.description: Army green knit polo — the spring fintech uniform
office.stylist_note: Go with a French tuck — back and sides tucked, a small front section left out. It reads intentional, not messy. Match the cognac belt to your shoes exactly. The army green/stone combo is an earth-tone spring move that reads elevated and easy simultaneously.

office.name: The Warm Day OCBD
office.description: Light blue oxford and navy trousers — quietly sharp
office.stylist_note: Leave the OCBD partially untucked in the French tuck style — back tucked, front loose. Open two shirt buttons at the collar. No undershirt visible. The light blue/navy combination is intentionally coastal — exactly the right signal for a warm NYC office day.

office.name: The Merino Polo Day
office.description: Slate blue merino polo and stone chinos — the clean spring formula
office.stylist_note: Merino polo tucked in, full tuck. One collar button open. Stone chinos with a clean break. Dark suede derbies add texture without weight. This is a one-degree-nicer version of khaki-and-polo that reads fintech rather than golf club.

office.name: The Navy Pique Office
office.description: Navy pique polo and stone trousers — unfussy and sharp
office.stylist_note: Navy pique polo, fully tucked. Two collar buttons open. Stone trousers pressed with a crease. Tan leather loafers. This is the look that requires zero decisions but telegraphs good taste — the fintech uniform done with intention.

office.name: The Sage Linen Office
office.description: Sage green linen shirt and navy trousers — spring color done right
office.stylist_note: Sage linen over navy slim trousers is a coastal-professional combination. French tuck the linen shirt — it's too relaxed for a full tuck. Two buttons open. Cognac loafers. Let the linen wrinkle a little: fighting it makes you look anxious.

weekend.name: The Port Casual
weekend.description: OCBD and khaki shorts — coastal prep in its natural habitat
weekend.stylist_note: Roll the shorts once at the hem — one clean 1.5-inch roll. Tuck the OCBD in the back and let the front hang loose. Boat shoes no-sock. This is exactly the effortless coastal look that reads right in Port Washington — confident and uncontrived.

weekend.name: The Spring Saturday
weekend.description: Stripe tee and chinos — the casual formula that always lands
weekend.stylist_note: Untucked stripe tee, clean. Roll the chinos to mid-ankle — one and a half turns is exactly right. White sneakers keep it young. This outfit signals effortless taste — the stripe tee is doing significant style work for zero effort.

weekend.name: The Linen Casual
weekend.description: Cream linen shirt and dark jeans — relaxed but composed
weekend.stylist_note: Cream linen shirt untucked over dark slim jeans is a quietly elevated casual move. Leave two or three buttons open. White leather sneakers. The contrast of the relaxed linen against dark fitted denim creates casual tension that looks effortless.

weekend.name: The Terry Polo Dad
weekend.description: Light blue terry polo and stone chinos — warm-weather casual with texture
weekend.stylist_note: Terry polo, half-tucked. Stone slim chinos rolled once at the ankle. White cup-sole sneakers. The textured terry fabric does the work — everything else is clean and simple. This outfit reads relaxed resort energy without trying to be a resort outfit.

weekend.name: The Sweatshirt Saturday
weekend.description: Oatmeal crewneck and dark jeans — the weekend standard elevated
weekend.stylist_note: Heavy no-logo oatmeal crewneck, slightly oversized but not boxy. Dark slim jeans — the slim cut prevents it from reading too casual. Roll the jeans once. White leather sneakers. This is the look that requires no effort and looks like all the effort.

office.name: The Linen Summer
office.description: White linen and navy — summer power without the sweat
office.stylist_note: Linen wrinkles — embrace it, don't fight it. French tuck the OCBD so the front drapes naturally. Leave two collar buttons open. Linen trousers with tobacco suede loafers is a considered warm-weather power move that fintech offices don't see enough of.

office.name: The Navy Linen Office
office.description: Navy linen shirt and stone linen trousers — the full linen summer suit alternative
office.stylist_note: Navy linen over stone linen is a deliberate tone-on-tone approach to summer dressing. French tuck. Two collar buttons open. Tan leather loafers. This outfit reads as though you planned a summer capsule, which you did.

office.name: The Summer Polo
office.description: Light grey merino polo and stone slim trousers — cool and controlled
office.stylist_note: Light grey merino polo is a summer stealth move — it reads dressy from a distance, wears like a t-shirt. Full tuck, one button open. Stone slim trousers pressed. Cognac suede loafers add warmth to the grey. Understated and unmistakably considered.

office.name: The Sage Shirt Office
office.description: Sage green linen OCBD and white linen trousers — summer color confidence
office.stylist_note: Sage linen over white linen trousers is a risk that pays off. Full French tuck, three buttons open. White leather derbies. Keep accessories minimal — one watch. This is a fintech summer look that reads fashion-aware without looking like you're trying.

office.name: The Sky Blue Office
office.description: Sky blue linen OCBD and white slim trousers — effortlessly coastal professional
office.stylist_note: Sky blue and white is a summer classic for a reason. French tuck. Two collar buttons open. White leather loafers. This is the look that makes people assume you sailed here. Allow yourself one seasonal flourish: a woven belt in tan or cognac if you want it.

weekend.name: The Hot Saturday
weekend.description: Camp collar and linen shorts — resort energy without going full tourist
weekend.stylist_note: Leave the camp collar fully open — that's the entire silhouette. No tuck. Espadrilles add quiet summer sophistication over flip-flops. This outfit says you know what you're doing on a hot Saturday in Port Washington.

weekend.name: The LIRR Summer
weekend.description: Clean and breezy for hot transit days into the city
weekend.stylist_note: The light blue tee and white shorts combination is deceptively intentional — navy/white is a palette, not an accident. Keep the sneakers pristine. Sunglasses on the collar (not on the head). This outfit reads understated summer confidence.

weekend.name: The Navy Camp
weekend.description: Navy camp collar shirt and cream linen shorts — the summer uniform perfected
weekend.stylist_note: Navy camp collar fully open over a plain white tee underneath. Cream linen shorts with one light roll at the hem. White leather sneakers. Sunglasses. This is three-ingredient summer dressing: camp collar, shorts, clean shoes. Nothing more needed.

weekend.name: The Pale Yellow Weekend
weekend.description: Pale yellow terry polo and light linen shorts — summer color done quietly
weekend.stylist_note: Pale yellow is the summer color that confident dressers reach for while everyone else plays it safe. Terry polo untucked, light khaki linen shorts. White canvas sneakers. This is the outfit that photographs beautifully and wears even better at an outdoor table in Port.

weekend.name: The Stripe Linen Weekend
weekend.description: Short-sleeve stripe oxford and stone linen shorts — coastal confidence
weekend.stylist_note: Stripe short-sleeve oxford, two buttons open, untucked. Stone linen shorts with one small roll at the hem. Tan leather sandals — the only time sandals work is when everything else is intentional. This outfit belongs at a waterfront lunch in Port Washington.
